αἴης: αἶα — land, earth; gen. sg., epic by-form of γαῖα
βαθείης: βαθύς — deep; fem. gen. sg., epic -είης (= Attic -είας)
βαθὺ: βαθύς — deep, thick, heavy; neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’deep-standing’ (of a crop)
βαρείῃ: βαρύς — heavy, weighty; fem. dat. sg., Ionic -είῃ (= Attic βαρείᾳ)
βασιλῆες: βασιλεύς — king; nom. pl., epic βασιλῆες (= Attic βασιλεῖς)
βουλῆς: βουλή — counsel, plan, design; fem. gen. sg., Ionic η (= Attic βουλῆς), with ἐξήρχετο
γαῖα: γαῖα — earth, land; fem. nom. sg. (epic = Attic γῆ)
γλαφυρῆς: γλαφυρός — hollow, hollowed; fem. gen. sg.
δεῦρ: δεῦρο — hither, here; adv., elided (δεῦρ’ = δεῦρο)
δοῦρα: δόρυ — tree-trunk, beam, timber; also spear-shaft, spear; neut. nom./acc. pl.
δῶκ: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (δῶκ’ = ἔδωκε)
δῶκεν: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδωκεν)
εἴπω: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. subj. 1 sg.
εἵατ: ἧμαι — sit; pres. 3 pl., epic εἵαται (= Attic κάθηνται), elided (εἵατ’ = εἵαται): ’sit’
εἶσι: εἶμι — go, come; pres. 3 sg. used with future sense: ’will come’ · also pres. 3 sg. with present force: ’goes, ranges’ (Ἄρτεμις εἶσι κατ’ οὔρεα ’Artemis ranges over the mountains’)
εὐρέα: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα ’broad backs’ (ἐπ’ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης ’over the broad back of the sea’) · also masc. acc. sg., epic by-form of εὐρύν, agreeing with a masc. noun (θαλάσσης εὐρέα κόλπον ’the sea’s broad bosom’) · also neut. nom. pl., agreeing with θύρετρα ’doors’: καὶ εὐρέα περ ἐόντα ’wide though they are’
εὖρός: Εὖρος — the East Wind, personified; masc. nom. sg., accented εὖρός before a following enclitic (τε)
ζέφυρος: Ζέφυρος — Zephyr, the west wind; masc. nom. sg.
θεράποντες: θεράπων — attendant, servant; masc. nom. pl.
κάμε: κάμνω — grow weary, tire; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔκαμε)
κάρηνα: κάρηνον (pl. of κάρη) — head; in the plural, mountain peaks; neut. acc. pl.
καθ: κατά (elided καθ’) — down, throughout; prep. + acc., aspirated before rough breathing
κακὴν: κακός — bad, evil; fem. acc. sg. (ἔριν ... κακήν ’evil strife’)
κατένευσεν: κατανεύω — nod assent, promise by a nod; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable
κελεύει: κελεύω — bid, urge, order; pres. 3 sg.
κονίη: κονία — dust; fem. nom. sg., Ionic -η (= Attic -α)
κρονίδης: Κρονίδης — son of Cronus (Zeus); masc. nom. sg., patronymic
κὰδ: κατά (apocope κάδ before δ-) — down through, throughout; prep./preverb in tmesis: ’throughout the halls’ (κὰδ δώματα = κατὰ δώματα) · also a bare preverb in tmesis with a verb: κὰδ ... ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε ’threw down’
λέλυνται: λύω — loose, undo; perf. 3 pl. pass.: ’are loosened’
λαερτιάδη: Λαερτιάδης — son of Laertes, patronymic of Odysseus; voc. sg.
λαός: λαός — people, host, band of followers; masc. nom. sg.
λεῖπε: λείπω — leave, leave behind; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔλειπε)
μεγάροις: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. pl.: ‘in the halls’
μελαίνης: μέλας, μέλαινα — black, dark; fem. gen. sg.
μετηύδα: μεταυδάω — speak among, address (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg.
μηδ: μηδέ — and not, nor; neg. conj., elided (μηδ’ = μηδέ)
μὰψ: μάψ — idly, to no purpose, recklessly; adv.
μῆτιν: μῆτις — cunning intelligence, craft, counsel; fem. acc. sg.
νέεσθαι: νέομαι — go, return home; pres. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic νεῖσθαι)
νήεσσι: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. pl., epic νήεσσι (= Attic ναυσί)
νήπια: νήπιος — without sense, foolish, childish; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’foolish things’ · also neut. nom. pl., attributive: ’infant, little’ (νήπια τέκνα ’infant children’) · also neut. acc. pl., attributive, object of ἄγον: ’infant, little’ (νήπια τέκνα ’infant children’)
νήσοισι: νῆσος — island; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
νηῶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. pl., epic νηῶν (= Attic νεῶν)
νόστος: νόστος — homecoming, return; masc. nom. sg.
νότος: Νότος — the South Wind, personified; masc. nom. sg.
νῶτα: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. pl. νῶτα, poetic image ’the broad back(s) of the sea’ · also ’back’ of a person: ’his back’ (ἥ οἱ νῶτα … ἄμπεχεν) · also the backs of animals: ’backs’ (ὀίων … νῶτα)
οἴκαδε: οἶκος — house, home; + directional suffix -δε: ’homeward, to one’s home’
παντὶ: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. sg.: ’to everyone’ (or ’to everything’) · also agreeing with a noun: ’whole, all of’ (παντὶ μετώπῳ ’with the whole forehead’)
πατρίδα: πατρίς — native land, fatherland; fem. acc. sg. (φίλην ... πατρίδα γαῖαν ’his dear fatherland’)
πατρίδος: πατρίς — fatherland, native land; gen. sg.
πειθώμεθα: πείθω — persuade; mid. obey, + dat.; pres. subj. mid. 1 pl., hortatory: ’let us obey’
πιστὰ: πιστός — trustworthy, to be trusted; neut. nom. pl., ἐστί understood: οὐκέτι πιστά ’no longer is there trust’ · also neut. acc. pl., attributive: ’faithful, trusty’ (ὅρκια πιστά ’faithful oaths’)
ποιμένι: ποιμήν — shepherd; masc. dat. sg., in the standing royal title ποιμὴν λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’
πολλέων: πολύς — much, many; fem. gen. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic πολλῶν)
πολλαί: πολύς — much, many; fem. nom. pl.: ’many’
πολυμήχαν: πολυμήχανος — many-devising; voc. sg., elided (πολυμήχαν’ = πολυμήχανε)
πολὺν: πολύς — much, many; masc. acc. sg., acc. of duration: ’for a long time’ · also adjectival, agreeing with a direct object noun: ‘much’ (πολὺν βίοτον ‘much livelihood’)
προπάροιθε: προπάροιθε — before, in front of; adv./prep. + gen.
πτόλιν: πτόλις (epic by-form of πόλις) — city; acc. sg.
πυθέσθαι: πυνθάνομαι — inquire, learn, hear of; aor. inf. mid. πυθέσθαι, epexegetic: ’to hear of’ (κλέος ... πυθέσθαι ’fame ... to hear of’) · also aor. inf. mid., of purpose after a verb of sending: ’to inquire’ (προέμεν πυθέσθαι ’to send forth to inquire’)
πόντου: πόντος — sea, open sea; masc. gen. sg.
πᾶσ: πᾶς — all, whole; fem. nom. sg., elided (πᾶσ’ = πᾶσα), of Charybdis: ’all of her’
σκηπτοῦχοι: σκηπτοῦχος — sceptre-bearing, sceptred; masc. nom. pl., also as a noun: ’the sceptre-bearers’
σπουδῇ: σπουδή — haste, effort, zeal; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ‘with effort, barely’ · also fem. dat. sg. adverbial, ’in haste, hurriedly’ (σπουδῇ νῦν ἀνάβαινε ’now go aboard in haste’)
στεναχίζετο: στεναχίζω — groan, sigh, resound with groaning; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented
σφεας: σφεῖς — they; epic acc. pl. pron.: ’them’
σφισιν: σφεῖς — they; epic dat. pl. pron. (= Attic αὐτοῖς): ’to/for them’
σχέτλιος: σχέτλιος — cruel, merciless, hard-hearted; masc. nom. sg. (applied here to Zeus, an unusually harsh judgment of a god) · also of sleep: ’cruel’ (ὕπνος σχέτλιος)
τέλος: τέλος — end, completion, fulfilment; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ταμόντες: τάμνω (τέμνω) — cut; aor. part. masc. nom. pl., epic τάμνω (= Attic τεμόντες): ’having cut’
τοιόνδε: τοιόσδε — such as this, of this kind; neut. acc. sg.
τρῶές: Τρώς — Trojan; masc. nom. pl. Τρῶες, accented before the enclitic τε
φίλης: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. gen. sg.
φεύγωμεν: φεύγω — flee; pres. subj. 1 pl., hortatory: ’let us flee’
φημι: φημί — say, declare, assert; pres. 1 sg.
φορῆναι: φορέω — carry, bring; pres. inf., epic -ῆναι (= Attic φορεῖν)
φῶτα: φώς — man, mortal; masc. acc. sg.
ἀΐξασα: ἀΐσσω — dart, rush; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg.
ἀγέροντο: ἀγείρω — gather, assemble; aor. 3 pl. mid., unaugmented, epic (= ἠγέροντο): ’gathered’
ἀγανοῖς: ἀγανός — gentle, mild; adj., neut. dat. pl., agreeing with βελέεσσιν
ἀγορήν: ἀγορή — assembly, gathering-place; fem. acc. sg. (Attic ἀγορά)
ἀγορὴ: ἀγορή — assembly; fem. nom. sg. (Attic ἀγορά)
ἀγχοῦ: ἀγχοῦ — near, close by; adv. (by-form of ἄγχι)
ἀκράαντον: ἀκράαντος — unaccomplished, unfulfilled, vain; fem. acc. sg. (2-termination adj., predicative): ’in vain’
ἀλαλητῷ: ἀλαλητός — war-cry, shout; masc. dat. sg., of manner
ἀλλήλοισι: ἀλλήλων — one another; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι
ἀμφιελίσσας: ἀμφιέλισσα — curved at both ends (standing epithet of ships); fem. acc. pl.
ἀνδράσι: ἀνήρ — man; masc. dat. pl., epic ἀνδράσι
ἀπονέεσθαι: ἀπονέομαι — go back, return; pres. inf.
ἀπόλοντο: ἀπόλλυμι — destroy; mid. ἀπόλλυμαι, perish, be lost, die; aor. 3 pl.: ’perished’
ἀργείην: Ἀργεῖος — Argive, of Argos; adj., fem. acc. sg., epic -είην (= Attic Ἀργείαν)
ἀργείοισιν: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Achaeans/Greeks; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀργεϊφόντῃ: ἀργεϊφόντης — Argeïphontes, epithet of Hermes, of unknown or disputed meaning; masc. dat. sg.
ἀργεῖοι: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀτρυτώνη: Ἀτρυτώνη — Atrytone, cult-title of Athena, traditionally ’the Unwearied’, though the derivation is uncertain; fem. voc./nom. sg.
ἁδινάων: ἁδινός — thronging, close-packed, clamorous (sense debated); adj., fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (Attic -ῶν)
ἄγεθ: ἄγετε (elided ἄγεθ’) — come now! (interjectional imperative of ἄγω); 2 pl.
ἄπο: ἀπό — away from, from; + gen.; accented ἄπο when it follows its noun (anastrophe: φίλων ἄπο) · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ὀλέσαντ’ ἄπο = ἀπολέσαντα ’having lost’)
ἄπρηκτον: ἄπρηκτος — without remedy, not to be dealt with; two-ending adj., fem. acc. sg., with ἀνίην
ἄργος: Ἄργος — Argos, the Argive plain; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also Ἄργος — Argus, Odysseus’s hound; masc. nom. sg. (the dog’s name)
ἄρηος: Ἄρης — Ares, god of war; also war, battle; masc. gen. sg., epic Ἄρηος (= Attic Ἄρεως)
ἅπτεσθαι: ἅπτομαι — take hold of, lay hold of (+ gen.); pres. inf. mid.
ἐθέλοντα: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’willing’ (οὐκ ἐθέλοντα ’not willing, unwillingly’)
ἐπεσσεύοντο: ἐπισεύομαι — hurry on, rush to; impf. 3 pl. mid., epic -σσ- (= Attic ἐπεσεύοντο): ’hastened to’
ἐρήτυε: ἐρητύω — hold back, restrain; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἠρήτυε)
ἐρήτυον: ἐρητύω — hold back, restrain; impf. 3 pl.: ’were holding back’
ἐσσεύοντο: σεύω — set moving; mid. rush, hasten; impf. 3 pl. mid., epic augment with doubled σ (ἐσσ-)
ἐσσομένοισι: εἰμί — be; fut. part. masc. dat. pl., epic ἐσσομένοισι (= Attic ἐσομένοις): ’to those who are to be, future generations’
ἐτύχθη: τεύχω — make, bring about; aor. pass. 3 sg.: ‘came to pass’
ἐϋσσέλμοιο: ἐΰσσελμος — well-benched (of ships; σέλματα are the rowing-benches); fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἑλένην: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. acc. sg.
ἑλοίμεθα: αἱρέω — take; mid. choose; aor. opt. mid. 1 pl. (stem ἑλ-), potential with κεν: ’we would choose’ · also aor. opt. in a purpose clause after ὡς ἄν: ’we might seize’ (ὡς ἂν ἐπιθύσαντες ἑλοίμεθα ’so that, rushing in, we might seize’)
ἑρμείας: Ἑρμείας — Hermes, epic form of Ἑρμῆς; nom. sg.
ἑσταότ: ἵστημι — set; stand; perf. part. masc. acc. sg., elided (ἑσταότ’ = ἑσταότα, Attic ἑστηκότα): ’standing’ · also perf. part. masc. nom. dual, elided (ἑσταότ’ = ἑσταότε): ’the two standing’
ἔασιν: εἰμί — be; epic pres. 3 pl. (= Attic εἰσίν): ’are’
ἔθνεα: ἔθνος — tribe, throng, host; neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἔθνη)
ἔπ: ἐπί — on, upon; standing for ἔπεστι ’is there, is at hand’, accent thrown back (ἔπι), elided ἔπ’ · also adverbial ἔπ’ with no ἔπεστι sense (τόσσον ἔπ’ εὐρεῖαν), exact force debated · also ἐπί + dat. of cause, accent thrown back (ἔπ’ = ἔπι): ’for, on account of’ (τῷ ἔπ’ … μογήσῃ ’for whom he has toiled’)
ἔπε: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. acc. pl. (ἔπεα, elided ἔπε’), epic uncontracted (= Attic ἔπη)
ἔστη: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg. intrans.: ’stood, took his stand’
ἕδρας: ἕδρα — seat, session, company seated together; fem. acc. pl.
ἕκαστοι: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. nom. pl.: ’each of us’ · also masc. nom. pl., of a third party: ’each man’ (ἐπὶ κληῗσιν ἕκαστοι ’each man at his bench’)
ἕκαστον: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. acc. sg.
ἠΰτε: ἠΰτε — like as, even as; epic particle introducing a comparison
ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’
ἧς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. gen. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whose, of whom/which (fem. gen. sg.)
ἰκαρίοιο: Ἰκάριος — Icarius, father of Penelope; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἰλίου: Ἴλιος — Ilios, Troy; fem. gen. sg.
ἱεμένων: ἵεμαι — hasten, press on, be eager; pres. part. mid. gen. pl., epic: ‘hastening’, agreeing with εἰδώλων
ἱκόμεσθα: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive; aor. 1 pl. mid., epic -μεσθα (= Attic -μεθα): ’we came’
ἱσταμένη: ἵστημι — set, make stand; mid. stand, come to stand; pres. part. mid. fem. nom. sg.: ’coming to stand, standing’
ὀδυσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; acc. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆα)
ὄρινε: ὀρίνω — stir up, rouse; pres. imper. 2 sg., after μηδέ in a prohibition: ’do not stir up’ · also impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ὤρινε): ’he stirred’
ὄσσα: Ὄσσα — Rumour, report personified as a messenger; fem. nom. sg. (common noun ὄσσα ’voice, report’)
ὅρκια: ὅρκιον — oath, sworn pledge; neut. acc. pl.: ὅρκια δοῦναι ’give oaths, swear’
ὅσσοι: ὅσος — as much/many as; epic ὅσσος, masc. nom. pl.: ’as many as’ (correlative with τόσσοι)
ὑπένερθε: ὑπένερθε(ν) — below, underneath, beneath; adv., + gen.: ’below’ (ὑπένερθε Χίοιο ’below Chios’)
ὑπέσχετο: ὑπισχνέομαι — promise; aor. mid. 3 sg., augmented (ὑπο- + ἐ- elides to ὑπε-): ’promised’
ὢ: ὤ — oh! ah! (exclamation, as in ὢ πόποι)
ὤλεσα: ὄλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. 1 sg.: ’I destroyed’
ᾕρεον: αἱρέω — take, seize; impf. 3 pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ᾕρουν); with ἀπό in tmesis, ’they took away’
